replacement.content:

Escitalopram 10 mg once daily initially; increase by 10 mg after at least one week; maximum 20 mg/day. Older adults and hepatic/renal impairment require the guideline/label-specific adjustments.
Continuation: after remission on medication, continue the therapeutic dose for at least six months.

replacement.content:
Scope: outpatient adults with acute, subacute or chronic pain; excludes sickle-cell pain, cancer-related pain, palliative/end-of-life care and MOUD treatment.
Initial management: nonopioid therapies are preferred for subacute/chronic pain. Consider opioids only when expected functional/pain benefits outweigh risks. If starting an opioid, use an immediate-release product at the lowest effective dose.
Follow-up: for subacute/chronic pain, reevaluate benefits and risks within 1-4 weeks of opioid initiation or dosage escalation, then regularly. Safety: MME dose guideposts are not rigid limits. Use particular caution with concurrent benzodiazepines and evaluate combined risks rather than applying an automatic prohibition. Unless there is a life-threatening concern, avoid abrupt discontinuation or rapid dose reduction in physically dependent patients; changes should be individualized and collaborative. This guideline does not specify a universal second/third-line opioid or fixed titration percentage.

replacement.content: Zepbound (tirzepatide) is used with reduced-calorie eating and physical activity for adult weight reduction/maintenance and for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity. Start 2.5 mg subcutaneously weekly for 4 weeks; this is an initiation dose. Increase to 5 mg weekly, then by 2.5 mg after at least 4 weeks per dose as tolerated.
